RELATIONSHIP SCORING POLICY (bank internal)
+2  account age 3 years or more (+1 if 1-3 years, 0 if under 1 year)
+2  salary/inflow credited in at least 11 of the last 12 months (+1 if 9-10, 0 otherwise)
+2  average balance above Rs 50,000 (+1 if Rs 15,000-50,000, 0 below)
+2  previous loan fully repaid, never 30+ days late (+1 if repaid with 1-2 late months, 0 if no history)
-3  any cheque/direct-debit bounce in the last 12 months (per policy, applied once)
-4  any 90+ day delinquency on eCIB in the last 24 months
-6  any write-off or litigation flag on eCIB, ever
Decision bands: score >= 6 STRONG | 3-5 ACCEPTABLE | 0-2 THIN | below 0 POOR

Product on the shelf for proactive offers: Personal Instalment Loan: Rs 50,000-Rs 3,000,000, tenors 12/24/36/48 months, 28.3% p.a. (reducing rate), processing fee 2.0%, min income Rs 50,000
Bank policy: proactive offers only to STRONG or ACCEPTABLE relationships showing genuine cash stress; THIN gets monitoring; POOR gets no unsecured offer (secured/deposit-backed alternatives only). DBR cap 40%.

Should we proactively offer this customer a loan? Walk through the decision.

No unsecured offer. The score is -2 (POOR) driven by a cheque/DD bounce in the last 12 months, a write-off/litigation flag. The cash stress is real (16 days under Rs 5,000), which makes unsecured lending here more dangerous, not less - it would likely become another delinquency.

What we can responsibly put in front of them: deposit-backed finance against any savings, gold-backed finance if they hold gold, or a secured card with a small limit to start rebuilding the file. If the write-off is disputed, tell them the eCIB correction process through the reporting bank - a cleaned record reopens the normal shelf.

REQUEST
- Customer has asked for a Rs 410,000 personal loan (medical + school fees)
- Holds household gold they could pledge


How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores 3 (ACCEPTABLE) under policy, and lending unsecured into active delinquency markers sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

Work out the debt burden ratio and the verdict.
Passes. DBR with the new instalment is 34.8% against the 40% cap - (Rs 0 existing + Rs 21,206 new) on Rs 61,000 net income, leaving Rs 39,794 of monthly headroom after all obligations.

LOAN QUOTE
- Product: Microfinance Enterprise Loan
- Principal: Rs 260,000
- Tenor: 12 months
- Rate: 37.2% p.a. on a flat basis
- Processing fee: 1.0% upfront

Calculate the EMI and the all-in cost.

<think>
Step 1: flat markup = P x rate x years = 260,000 x 37.2% x 12/12 = Rs 96,720.
Step 2: EMI = (260,000 + 96,720) / 12 = Rs 29,727.
Step 3: total paid = Rs 29,727 x 12 = Rs 356,720; processing fee = 1.0% x 260,000 = Rs 2,600.
</think>

Instalment: Rs 29,727/month for 12 months.

- Total repaid: Rs 356,720
- Markup over the life: Rs 96,720
- Processing fee (upfront): Rs 2,600
- All-in cost above principal: Rs 99,320 One caution on flat-rate quotes: a flat rate charges markup on the full principal for the whole tenor even as you pay it down, so the effective reducing-balance rate is nearly double the sticker - compare quotes on total rupees paid, not the headline rate.

Apply each policy line:
- 2 of last 4 instalments paid late -> +pts

(no other lines trigger)

- 23 days under Rs 5,000 last month

Action: call before the next due date, offer a restructuring conversation now - pre-delinquency restructuring is cheap; post-default recovery is not. Do not wait for the 30-DPD letter.

MY RUNNING LOAN
- Original: Rs 1,440,000 over 36 months at 25.5% p.a. (reducing)
- Instalment: Rs 57,636/month
- Instalments paid so far: 13
- Outstanding principal today (per bank statement): Rs 1,040,041
- Early settlement fee: 3% of outstanding principal
- I have a bonus in hand and can pay it all off now.

What do I save by closing this loan today?

<think>
Step 1: staying the course = Rs 57,636 x 23 remaining instalments = Rs 1,325,620.
Step 2: settling today = outstanding Rs 1,040,041 + 3% fee Rs 31,201 = Rs 1,071,242.
Step 3: saving = Rs 1,325,620 - Rs 1,071,242 = +254,378 PKR.
</think>

Yes - settle. Closing today costs Rs 1,071,242 against Rs 1,325,620 of remaining instalments, a saving of Rs 254,378 (the future markup you no longer pay, net of the 3% fee).

Two practical points: get a written settlement quote valid for a date (the outstanding moves with each cycle), and after payment collect the loan clearance letter and confirm the facility is reported closed on eCIB - that closed line is what improves your file for the next time you borrow.

- Product: Gold-backed Finance at 22.4% p.a. (reducing), tenor 36 months

Size the gold-backed facility.

<think>
Step 1: assessed value = 14.7 tola x Rs 250,000 x 22/24 purity = Rs 3,368,750.
Step 2: max loan at 70% LTV = Rs 2,358,125.
Step 3: request Rs 2,860,000 vs cap Rs 2,358,125 -> grant Rs 2,350,000.
Step 4: instalment on Rs 2,350,000 at 22.4% over 36 months = Rs 90,235.
</think>

The gold values at Rs 3,368,750 (14.7 tola adjusted to 22K), supporting a maximum of Rs 2,358,125 at 70% LTV.

That falls Rs 510,000 short of the Rs 2,860,000 requested - grant Rs 2,350,000 and let them bridge the gap elsewhere or add more gold to the pledge. Instalment on Rs 2,350,000: Rs 90,235/month for 36 months.

Worth telling the customer: because the pledge secures the facility, this prices at 22.4% against ~30%+ for unsecured personal loans, approval does not hinge on the bureau file, and the gold comes back on full settlement. The risk to flag honestly is the margin call - if gold prices fall sharply, the bank can ask for partial prepayment or extra pledge to restore the LTV.

I need Rs 1,070,000 for 12 months. Three quotes on the table:

| Offer | Rate | Processing fee |
|---|---|---|
| Offer A | 31.7% reducing | 2.0% |
| Offer B | 23.4% reducing | 3.0% |
| Offer C | 12.3% flat | 1.0% |

Compare these on total rupees paid and pick one.

Offer C is cheapest at Rs 1,212,310 all-in - Rs 71,586 less than the most expensive quote.

- Offer A: EMI Rs 105,208 (reducing) -> total Rs 1,262,496 + fee Rs 21,400 = Rs 1,283,896
- Offer B: EMI Rs 100,868 (reducing) -> total Rs 1,210,420 + fee Rs 32,100 = Rs 1,242,520
- Offer C: flat markup Rs 131,610, EMI Rs 100,134 -> total Rs 1,201,610 + fee Rs 10,700 = Rs 1,212,310

The trap to avoid: a flat rate applies markup to the full Rs 1,070,000 for all 12 months even as the balance falls, so a 12.3% flat sticker is roughly double that in reducing-balance terms. Total rupees is the only fair comparison.

CUSTOMER PROFILE
- Name: Nadeem Hussain, 60
- Bank: Sindh Bank (SNDB), Lahore
- Employment: Netsol Technologies (permanent)
- Verified net monthly income: Rs 156,000
- Account age: 2.4 years
- Salary/inflow months (last 12): 10/12

- Previous loan: no prior loan history
- Cheque/DD bounce in last 12 months: no
- eCIB 90+ DPD in last 24 months: no
- eCIB write-off/litigation flag: no
- Existing monthly obligations: none

SITUATION
- Running loan: originally Rs 870,000 at 26.5%, 10 of 48 instalments paid, outstanding Rs 755,399, instalment Rs 29,579
- Income has dropped 50% (Rs 156,000 -> Rs 78,000) after contract non-renewal
- Instalments missed so far: 2
- Bank restructuring option on the table: extend remaining tenor by 18 months at the same rate
- DBR cap: 40%

Does the restructuring actually fix the affordability problem? What does it cost?

<think>
Step 1: DBR before the income shock = (0 + 29,579) / 156,000 = 19.0%.
Step 2: same instalment on the new income = 37.9% -> clearly unaffordable.
Step 3: restructured instalment = EMI on 755,399 over 56 months at 26.5% = Rs 23,638.
Step 4: DBR after restructuring = (0 + 23,638) / 78,000 = 30.3% -> inside the 40% cap.
Step 5: cost of the relief = extra markup Rs 199,715 over the extended life.
</think>

Take it - it works. The extension drops the instalment from Rs 29,579 to Rs 23,638, bringing DBR from an unpayable 37.9% down to 30.3% on the reduced income.

The honest price tag: about Rs 199,715 of additional markup over the extra 18 months. That is real money, but it is cheaper than the alternative - 2 missed instalments become 90+ DPD on eCIB, and a spoiled bureau record costs far more than Rs 199,715 over a lifetime of borrowing. Get the revised schedule in writing and ask the bank to report the facility as 'restructured - regular', not delinquent, once the new schedule is running.

SALARY ADVANCE PRODUCT
- Limit: up to 2.0x of net monthly salary
- Fee: 1.5% of amount | Markup: 29.5% p.a. (flat) | Tenor: 1 month(s)
- Eligibility: salary credited in at least 10 of the last 12 months to this account

Is this customer eligible, how much can they take, and what will it cost?

<think>
Step 1: eligibility gate - salary in 9/12 months, policy needs 10+ -> fails at the gate.
</think>

Decline for this product: salary landed in only 9 of the last 12 months against the 10-month requirement - a salary advance is repaid by the next salary, so irregular inflows are the one thing it cannot tolerate.

Alternatives that fit irregular income: a nano loan sized to a single month, or gold/deposit-backed finance if collateral exists. And if the salary irregularity is an employer-side delay, a letter from the employer plus 3 months of consistent credits reopens this product.
